fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Abdul El-Sayed Is an Epidemiologist Running for Senate. His State Is a Public Health Disaster - WIRED
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: These in-your-face (and sometimes in-your-gut) problems, says senatorial candidate Abdul El-Sayed, help make a complex topic—the need to invest in public health infrastructure—extremely easy to talk about with voters. I don’t like the idea because we DOGE’d our whole service that keeps the lettuce safe,” El-Sayed says, referring to how the Department of Government Efficiency downsized the federal lab that tests for cyclosporiasis last year. And if you don’t, then you’re stuck on a toilet for the next five days. WIRED caught up with El-Sayed to chat about how he’d fix the public health problems facing his state and why we shouldn’t accept that “poop lettuce” is our new normal. You think about the great DOGEing of a lot of our public health infrastructure—while it’s impossible to connect one outcome to the next, if you cut the staff of the people who are supposed to be invested in keeping us healthy, don’t be surprised when, down the line, they’re not good at keeping us healthy.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Cardiologists Say This Cheap Cholesterol Test Can Catch Risk LDL Tests Might Miss - Men's Health
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Make sure to ask about this cheap add-on at your next doctor’s visit. **WHEN IT COMES** to staying on top of your heart health, keeping track of your cholesterol numbers should be on the top of the list. So what’s the best way to do it? Turns out, the standard LDL cholesterol blood test millions get at the doctor’s office may not be enough. New research published in JAMA found that an alternative and cost-effective way to suss out high cholesterol is to use an ApoB test. The good news is that the test isn’t new. ## Why the ApoB Test Helps With Cholesterol Testing. By looking at the number of ApoB particles, you get a better read on just how much fatty lipid traffic there is in your arteries. They modeled what heart health outcomes would be over their lives if their doctors used one of three common tests to base treatment on: LDL cholesterol, non-HDL (“good”) cholesterol, and ApoB.

fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Bengaluru-based Even Healthcare is reportedly in advanced talks to raise $50 million, potentially doubling its valuation to $300 million. The startup, which operates a subscription-based model and hospital network, is looking to fund further expansion plans. Even Healthcare, a subscription-focused healthcare and insurance provider based in Bengaluru, is reportedly working toward a new Series B funding round of approximately $50 million. If completed, the deal is expected to value the startup at roughly $300 million. It launched its first hospital in Bengaluru last year and has stated plans to establish four to five additional hospitals by the end of the 2026 calendar year. For investors, the ability of the company to effectively scale this hospital network while maintaining service quality—such as patient readmission rates and stay durations—remains a key operational focus. The transition from a purely subscription-based digital health model to an asset-heavy hospital provider introduces execution risks, including the high capital requirements and the competitive intensity of the healthcare services market in India.

fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Here Are 10 Ways To Manage Your Health And Track Aging. Health tracking tools are increasingly accessible. High-value, cost-effective options include physical performance tests like grip strength and gait speed, and DEXA scans for body composition. Routine bloodwork can be enhanced with biomarkers such as ApoB and hsCRP. More advanced technologies like epigenetic clocks, proteomics, and full-body MRIs are promising but currently expensive and lack robust clinical evidence for routine use in healthy adults. But what health tracking data should be measured over time to see if your choices are actually making you healthier? Tools for tracking health and wellness, as of 2026, have never been more accessible and sophisticated. Tracking data in and of itself can often a first step to improved health.
